purpose: Independent public-data screen of the consequence-model thermal-effect boundary for an ignited high-pressure hydrogen release.

source.title: Experimental data- hydrogen safety, thermal effects
source.scope_note: Ignited high-pressure hydrogen releases in a semi-confined space; this is a consequence-model source, not a gaseous H70 station-to-vehicle fill trace.

selection_rule: Retain every public MAT experiment file in the Figshare record; do not select or exclude cases after inspecting numerical outcomes.

primary_observables: time-resolved thermal sensor channels that can be mapped to distance/location
peak and time-to-peak temperature or heat-flux observables when present
release/ignition timing fields when explicitly provided by the source
predeclared_analysis.primary_screen: For each eligible sensor channel, compare model and measured peak thermal effect and event-time error using source-reported units; retain all eligible channels and report missing mappings rather than imputing them.
predeclared_analysis.eligibility: A file is eligible only when its metadata expose a time base and at least one numeric thermal/consequence measurement with a documented unit or sensor label.
exclusions: No post-outcome case deletion, parameter fitting, dynamic time warping or undocumented smoothing.
Non-thermal channels may support timing/context but cannot be silently treated as temperature or heat flux.
A consequence screen cannot validate the station controller, fueling protocol, field safety distance or LLM effectiveness.
predeclared_analysis.claim_boundary: Independent consequence-model evidence only; it does not close the full-loop external validation gate or establish legal separation distances.

data_redistribution: The source remains external; retain metadata, hashes and derived summary only unless the CC BY terms and repository policy permit a copy.
